pass_a_gloss: Proskunein/latreuein split: tribunal deniers worship though they serve not; Belphegor and calf precedents.
pass_b_english: If he who says 'Thou shalt make thee no idol nor any likeness,' (Exodus 20:4–5) and what follows — wherein the 'thou shalt not worship them' differs from the 'nor shalt thou serve them' — says this, might not one disposed toward idols serve them, while one not disposed but, through cowardice — which he calls compliance — playing the hypocrite toward them to seem godly like the many, serve not but worship the idols? I would say those who on the tribunal deny Christianity, or before the tribunal, serve not but worship the idols — taking the name of the Lord God, 'God,' in vain upon soulless matter. So too the profaned people worshiped but served not idols, 'unto the daughters of Moab.' For it stands written in these very words that they called them to the sacrifices of their idols, and the people ate of their sacrifices, 'and worshiped their idols, and were joined to Belphegor.' (Numbers 25:1–3) And observe that it is not said 'and served their idols' — for it was not possible, under one season's moment, with such signs and wonders, to be persuaded by the women with whom they fornicated to deem the idols gods. Perhaps so too at the calf-making in Exodus they 'worshiped,' not serving the calf they saw coming to be.
